title: Internal Hom with finite Tor amplitude
statement:
Let $A=A_{E,n}$, let $X$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme with $\dim X\le m$, and
let $K,M$ be bounded constructible $A$-complexes on $X_{\Et}$ with finite Tor
amplitude in $[a,b]$ and in $[c,d]$. Then
$\RHom_A(K,M)$ is bounded constructible with finite Tor amplitude in
$[c-b-2m,d-a+2m]$. If $K$ is site-perfect, that is, dualizable (locally on
$X_{\Et}$ a bounded complex of finite projective $A$-modules in degrees
$[a,b]$), the sharper interval $[c-b,d-a]$ holds.

proof.text: If $m<0$, then $\dim X\le m$ forces $\dim X=-\infty$, so $X$ is empty by [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. The small etale site of the empty scheme has only the empty object, covered by the empty family, so every sheaf on it is zero; hence $K=M=0$ and $\RHom_A(K,M)=0$. The zero complex is bounded constructible, and every derived tensor product with it vanishes, so it has Tor amplitude in every interval; both conclusions hold. Assume from now on $m\geq0$. The existing split node [thm-sf-hom-ctf] proves the same finite-stage étale internal-Hom theorem. Instantiate its global finite-field datum with the $A=A_{E,n}$, $X$, dimension bound $m$, amplitudes $[a,b]$ and $[c,d]$, and complexes $K,M$ of this item; all hypotheses match the definitions in the statement. Its general clause gives bounded constructibility and the interval $[c-b-2m,d-a+2m]$, and its site-perfect clause gives the sharper interval $[c-b,d-a]$. That clause applies: the item's hypothesis, that locally on $X_{\Et}$ the complex $K$ is isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite projective $A$-module sheaves (direct summands of finite free ones) in degrees $[a,b]$, implies the cited theorem's site-perfect hypothesis by forgetting the degree bounds.
